thread:
devon: CI build failure for the new attention-kernels branch. saw crazy fatbin growth when adding sm_90 support. attaching excerpt from the job log

build-bot: [FAIL] kernel-packaging: artifact size 142.3MB (threshold 120MB) for runtime/kernels/fatbin-all-sm.cubin
```
[2024-04-05T09:12:34Z] + nvcc -O3 --fatbin -gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 ... -o fatbin-all-sm.cubin
[2024-04-05T09:12:58Z] linking fatbins -> fatbin-all-sm.cubin
[2024-04-05T09:13:02Z] resulting size 149,436,224 bytes
```

sasha: ugh, that matches local repro. most of the increase is duplicate PTX+SASS sections for each target. we currently ship a single fatbin with PTX for all and cubin for each sm. adding sm_90 added a whole new PTX chunk. :face_with_rolling_eyes:

jin: possible mitigations: 1) split artifacts by SM (produce separate cubin files per sm + minimal fatbin/metadata), 2) strip PTX for non-fallback targets, 3) change CI artifact gate to allow aggregated per-sm size instead of one monolithic threshold.

olga: splitting sounds promising but will complicate runtime deployment: scheduler would need to pick the right artifact per device and handle fallbacks. current runtime expects a single artifact path. that's an interface boundary change.

tim: can we instead keep single artifact but store PTX only for lowest-common-fallback (e.g., compute_80) and only cubins for others? tradeoff: we lose JIT fallback for newer archs if we remove PTX there, but cost savings are big.

devon: The attention kernels are performance-sensitive for L1/L2 usage; JIT sometimes improves perf on new hw. removing PTX might hurt perf for a small % of customers. need data.

qa-bot: perf-regression-run queued: https://ci.redwood-inference/devices/perf/17234 (will compare sm_90 cubin vs JIT-compiled PTX on sm_90)

sasha: Another option: produce a small "fallback-ptx" slice that only contains device-independent kernels (prefix/kernels that runtime will JIT for checkpoint-load paths) and keep tuned cubins for production fast-path. This reduces duplicate PTX amount.

jin: implementation notes I sketched in the build script:
```
# proposed nvcc invocations (split build)
nvcc -O3 -gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -c kernel_sm86.cu -o kernel_sm86.cubin
nvcc -O3 -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 -c kernel_sm90.cu -o kernel_sm90.cubin
# fallback PTX build
nvcc -O3 -ptx kernel_all.cu -o kernel_fallback.ptx
# package: metadata.json references per-sm cubins + optional fallback.ptx
```
This keeps per-sm cubins small and prevents duplicating PTX per cubin.

olga: packaging metadata + runtime loader change is doable. main worry: CI and deploy tooling assume a single artifact name. we need a small migration plan: - change packaging to output a zip with named files - update release pipeline to upload zip - runtime to accept zip and pick files.

devon: CI changes: we should update size gate check to sum only the production cubins (or checked-in whitelist) and treat fallback.ptx separately with a separate threshold. current gate is naive.

tim: also consider using `--ptxas-options=-v` to detect register pressure early and reduce incidental size from debug info, and `-Xlinker --strip-all`/objcopy --strip-unneeded on cubins to trim symbols.

jin: note: nvcc flags that helped in my local: `-Xptxas -v` (to inspect), `--generate-line-info` disabled, and `-Xcompiler -fvisibility=hidden`. but be careful: `-line-info` removal affects stack traces for dev builds.

sasha: action items?
- devon: open RFC/PR for packaging format change + runtime loader changes
- jin: prototype split-build in buildkite job and measure artifact sizes
- olga: update release pipeline to accept zip and add migration docs
- tim: run objcopy/strip experiments and report regressions
- qa-bot: run perf/regression when artifacts available

devon: +1. I'll open a short RFC and include a proposal to keep a tiny fallback PTX only when necessary. linking PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/312 (WIP)

build-bot: note: current CI failure: https://ci.redwood-inference/job/45678/log - re-run after branch `kernel-split` job is ready by jin.

jin: I'll push a branch with split artifacts by EOD, will also add a compare job that computes per-file sizes so CI can show a breakdown.

olga: if we go this route we should also add manifest versioning so older runtimes can still accept new zips (or gracefully error).

sasha: sounds good. small follow-up: add a lightweight lint to detect accidental inclusion of debug symbols in release cubins (`readelf -S` check)

devon: perfect. thanks team. keeping this thread for tracking until PR merges.

sasha: thanks — ping me when the split-build job is up so I can validate deploy on a staging pod.
